intro: Preference learning compares a chosen response with a rejected response. DPO measures how their relative log probabilities change from a reference policy.
task: Build the reference-adjusted preference margin and compute its stable logistic loss. Distinguish a policy favoring the chosen response from a policy improving that preference relative to its reference.
requirements: The four inputs are nonempty one-dimensional arrays of the same length, containing nonpositive sequence log probabilities. beta is a finite nonnegative scalar.
For each pair use margin=beta*((policy_chosen-policy_rejected)-(reference_chosen-reference_rejected)). Return mean(log(1+exp(-margin))) as a scalar.

Use a stable softplus/logaddexp calculation without clipping the loss or adding a probability epsilon. These are supplied sequence log probabilities; do not normalize the chosen and rejected values into a two-class distribution.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Subtract two log-odds differences
hints.body: The reference correction compares chosen versus rejected responses in the same order as the policy.

hints.title: Avoid taking log of a rounded sigmoid
hints.body: At a very negative margin, direct sigmoid evaluation can underflow to zero. Stable softplus retains the large loss.

explanation: When policy and reference have identical relative preferences, the margin is zero and the loss is log(2), even if both strongly favor the chosen response.
A larger positive adjusted margin reduces the loss. beta scales this margin; beta zero makes every pair have loss log(2). This operation alone does not train a language model.
Ported the upstream DPO margin to NumPy and replaced log(sigmoid(margin)) with stable logaddexp. Added explicit sequence-level inputs and original reference-shift fixtures.
